Section (bend_01.png): the registered scan lies on the blue FORMED profile on both sides of the bend line. It follows both sheet faces through the kink at x=0, the second kink near x=-10 mm, the curve out to x=-40 mm and the flange end return at about x=+11 mm. I measured the pixels: the scan's segment directions are about +12 deg left of the line and -12 deg right of it, so the bend is roughly 24 deg. The orange NOT_FORMED profile is nearly straight across the line (left segment about -13 deg) and sits 3.7, 7, 11 and 17 mm above the scan at x=-8, -15, -25 and -38 mm. The scan follows none of it. Raw scan in its own frame, with no CAD: the FRONT view independently shows a separate flange facet meeting the sloped region at an angled crease, so the result does not depend on the registration. One limit: the angle comes from a single section, so I give it only as about 24 deg. The formed/not-formed call itself is unambiguous.

At the same points the NOT_FORMED profile is 2.0 mm away at -4.5 mm, 4.4 mm at -9.5 mm, 9.1 mm at -19.5 mm and 13 mm at -29.5 mm. In the overlay ISO, TOP and FRONT views, the scan covers the whole flange strip with holes along the full length of the line, and its holes and free edge sit at the CAD positions. The only gap is an edge offset of about 1 mm, which fits normal scanner loss at sheet edges. So the bend is formed along its whole length. The scanned sheet is one straight run from x=-16 mm through the B1 locus to the free edge (slope about -3 deg, rms 0.16 mm about a single line). The raw views show no distinct crease along the strip, though they are low resolution and only supporting. Caveat: only one section is provided, and the label assumes it is representative; the overlay pattern suggests it is. Note for the recipe: the CAD models this feature as a joggle (2 creases), but the recipe lists only B1.
